title: Platform and hosting in one screen
rememberThis: C# is the language; .NET is the platform; ASP.NET Core is the web framework on the runtime.
SDK builds in CI; aspnet runtime image runs in production — not the SDK container.
WebApplication.CreateBuilder: register services, Build, configure middleware, Run.
Kestrel serves HTTP; put nginx or ALB in front for TLS — UseForwardedHeaders first.
ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT defaults to Production; never ship Swagger in Production.
bullets: Framework-dependent publish needs matching Microsoft.AspNetCore.App on the host; self-contained bundles the runtime.
Host.CreateApplicationBuilder for queue-only workers without Kestrel; WebApplication when you need HTTP.
appsettings.{Environment}.json layers over base json; env vars override with double-underscore keys.
launchSettings.json sets local URLs and Development env — it does not publish to Docker.
Express/NestJS middleware, routing, and DI map directly — blocking hurts differently on each runtime.
SIGTERM triggers IHostApplicationLifetime.ApplicationStopping — pass CancellationToken to SQS and Redis calls.

rows.label: Build vs run
rows.value: dotnet SDK (build) → published DLL → .NET runtime + Kestrel (execute)

rows.label: Entry point
rows.value: Program.cs — WebApplication.CreateBuilder, no Startup.cs in modern templates

rows.label: Production edge
rows.value: Reverse proxy (nginx, IIS, ALB) → Kestrel :8080 with forwarded headers

rows.label: Node analog
rows.value: Express app ≈ WebApplication; NestJS modules ≈ DI extensions; NODE_ENV ≈ ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT

rows.label: Diagnostics
rows.value: Log startup duration; dotnet-counters for Kestrel connections and thread pool under load
